stem: When counseling a kidney candidate about the benefits of transplantation compared with remaining on dialysis, which outcome should the coordinator include in standard risk-and-benefit teaching?

options.text: Pre-emptive kidney transplantation may significantly benefit patients with ESRD through less time on dialysis
Dialysis always provides better long-term outcomes than any transplant option
Transplantation eliminates all future need for any medical follow-up
Living donation is never an option once dialysis has started

explanation.rationale_correct: Living donor transplant education includes that patients with ESRD benefit significantly with pre-emptive kidney transplantation and less time on dialysis.

rationale_incorrect.B: Transplantation, including pre-emptive kidney transplant, is presented as beneficial compared with prolonged dialysis for appropriate candidates.
rationale_incorrect.C: Transplant recipients require lifelong follow-up and monitoring rather than eliminating medical care.
rationale_incorrect.D: Living donation remains an option for many dialysis patients when a suitable donor is available.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 7, Care of Living Donors → Introduction → 6.b.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: patients with ESRD benefit significantly with pre-emptive kidney transplantation and less time on dialysis

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 7 → Introduction → 6.b. (pre-emptive kidney transplantation and less time on dialysis); PDF p. 331 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Sixth 010100 item; pre-emptive transplant benefit angle distinct from rejection/primary nonfunction/waitlist death; anchor verified on Cupples p. 331.

stem: A potential living liver donor asks how surgical risk compares with living kidney donation. Which teaching point aligns with standard living donor education?

options.text: Liver donation carries a higher risk than kidney donation but may still be performed at experienced centers
Liver donation has no measurable surgical risk compared with kidney donation
Kidney donation always carries higher perioperative risk than liver donation
Living liver donation is prohibited at all U.S. transplant centers

explanation.rationale_correct: Medical outcomes show that although liver donation portends a higher risk than kidney donation, it is still believed to be safe enough to perform at experienced centers.

rationale_incorrect.B: Liver donation is associated with higher risk than kidney donation rather than identical risk.
rationale_incorrect.C: References describe liver donation as higher risk than kidney donation, not the reverse.
rationale_incorrect.D: Living liver donation is performed at experienced centers when appropriate.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 7, Care of Living Donors → Introduction → 5.

stem: When explaining why living donor organs may offer advantages over some deceased-donor options, which donor characteristic should the coordinator emphasize?

options.text: The organ is typically from a young healthy person who completed an intensive medical evaluation
Living donors are never medically evaluated before donation
Deceased-donor organs always function better than any living-donor organ
Living donation eliminates the need for any immunosuppression after transplant

explanation.rationale_correct: Living donor transplant benefits include an organ from a typically young healthy person who has undergone an intense medical evaluation.

rationale_incorrect.B: Living donors undergo intensive medical evaluation before donation.
rationale_incorrect.C: Living donor organs may offer advantages related to donor health and timing rather than deceased donors always functioning better.
rationale_incorrect.D: Recipients still require immunosuppression after living donor transplantation.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 7, Care of Living Donors → Introduction → 6.a.

stem: When describing how living donors are protected during the donation process, what organizational feature should the coordinator explain?

options.text: A separate live donor team advocates on the donor's behalf
The recipient's surgeon exclusively represents both recipient and donor without a separate team
Donors have no structured program contact after the operative decision is made
Living donor advocacy is optional and prohibited by OPTN policy

explanation.rationale_correct: The hospital created a separate live donor team to advocate on the live organ donor's behalf, distinct from the recipient transplant team.

rationale_incorrect.B: A separate live donor team exists specifically to advocate for the donor rather than sole representation by the recipient surgeon.
rationale_incorrect.C: Living donor programs include structured advocacy and follow-up rather than no program contact.
rationale_incorrect.D: Separate live donor team advocacy is part of standard living donation practice, not prohibited.
